memory_update.text: SXT should be carried forward as the highest-priority underfollowed direct supplier for natural colors, flavors, extracts, and clean-label reformulation inputs; key survival tests are Color Group mix, natural-color capacity, Biolie integration, and regulatory-driven order evidence.
INGR should be tracked as a clean-label formulation and texture-input candidate, but not as a pure synthetic-dye replacement play; verify T&HS contribution and clean-label volume growth.

NEOG belongs in a second-order testing/certification-gate lane; its relevance depends on whether reformulation increases QA, allergen, residue, and food-quality testing demand enough to offset company-specific integration issues.

Private and non-US-listed ingredient leaders such as Kalsec, Givaudan, Symrise, and other European specialty ingredient companies may define competitive pricing and capacity, but this pass is restricted to US-listed public candidates.

node: Natural colors, flavors, extracts, and clean-label reformulation inputs
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around clean-label reformulation inputs. The highest-relevance underfollowed name is Sensient Technologies because it has direct color, flavor, extract, and natural-color extraction exposure. Ingredion adds a clean-label texture and specialty ingredient lane. Neogen is a second-order testing and food-safety gate tied to reformulation validation rather than ingredient supply. IFF is included as a larger reference competitor/context anchor, not the primary underfollowed target. No buy/sell view is implied.
